# PulseDB 0.5.1 legacy collective oracle

This directory holds the immutable pre-upgrade oracle for the PulseDB 0.7
migration (Release 1 exit criterion 5): a real collective database written by
PulseHive 2.0.2 crates against `pulsehive-db` 0.5.1, checked in so that the
migration work item (`r1.s4.w3`) must migrate these exact bytes and prove a
consumer still perceives the recorded experiences.

## Why the `v2.0.2` tag is not the source

The published tag `v2.0.2` is an annotated tag: `git rev-parse v2.0.2` names
the tag object `0969c8e330b95b0125339ab3a9b108d1ba8fe82c` (type `tag`), not a
commit. Peeling it to the commit actually tagged —
`git rev-parse 'v2.0.2^{commit}'` — yields
`eda134f7517ba3709200646fa47f870432b80dd7`, and that commit's dependency
graph pins PulseDB 0.4. The first PulseHive 2.0.2-crate commit that requires
`pulsehive-db = "0.5"` is canonical commit `a9f7839`
(`a9f783989ccb4d12eda9f4e5bd3318ef4e3df7ae`), and Cargo resolves that
requirement to `pulsehive-db` 0.5.1. The fixture therefore names `a9f7839` as
its generator commit and 2.0.2 / 0.5.1 as its crate versions — not the tagged
release.

## How the bytes were made

A temporary checkout of `a9f7839` was materialized with
`git archive a9f7839 | tar -x`. Into it, `generate.rs` (checked in next to
this README, verbatim) was placed at
`pulsehive-runtime/examples/generate_legacy_fixture.rs` and run once with:

```text
cargo run --example generate_legacy_fixture
```

The generator builds a `HiveMind` with only `substrate_path(...)` set. At 2.0.2
that opens PulseDB with `Config::with_builtin_embeddings()` — the builtin
all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding mode, no external provider — so PulseDB 0.5.1
computes embeddings internally for every experience recorded with
`embedding: None`. The default relationship detector and insight synthesizer
were left enabled, so the bytes come from the unmodified real PulseHive
path. The run printed a JSON provenance document (collective id, per-experience
ids, generated timestamps) that became `manifest.json`; ids and timestamps are
generated by 0.5.1 and captured there rather than pretended to be reproducible.
The database file was then copied here byte-for-byte as `collective.db`.

## Why tests must copy the database before opening it

`collective.db` is a checked-in oracle: its SHA-256 is pinned in
`manifest.json` and the migration proof in `r1.s4.w3` depends on these exact
bytes. Opening a PulseDB database can write (WAL/journal files, metadata,
compaction on close), so the checked-in file must never be a writable target.
Every test that reads this fixture first copies `collective.db` to a temporary
directory and opens only the copy; the baseline test
(`pulsehive-runtime/tests/pulsedb_legacy_fixture.rs`) additionally asserts the
checked-in bytes are unchanged after its run, and the work-item gate
re-verifies the SHA-256 with `shasum -a 256` before and after.

## What the migration must preserve

Work item `r1.s4.w3` must keep observable, per experience: `content`,
`importance`, `confidence`, `domain`, `related_files`, `source_agent`, and a
non-empty 384-dimension embedding (builtin mode); and at the collective level:
the collective's identity by name. Every pinned value is recorded in
`manifest.json`, which is the semantic oracle the migration asserts against.
The database here is synthetic data only — no production or user content.

## Files

- `collective.db` — the immutable database bytes (SHA-256 in `manifest.json`).
- `manifest.json` — schema version 1 provenance: generator commit, crate
  versions, SHA-256, collective name/id, every seeded experience
  id/content/importance/confidence/domain, and the exact generator invocation.
- `generate.rs` — the deterministic one-shot generator source, retained as
  provenance; it is **not** compiled by the current workspace (nothing under
  `tests/fixtures/` is a cargo target).
